architecture.mechanism: Vacuum-assisted pressure gradient engineering to drive fluid flow through a resistive pathway according to Darcy's law.
architecture.intervention: Integrate a controlled vacuum source at the distal outlet of the multi-lumen medical tubing to establish a sustained negative pressure gradient across the lumen length, actively driving fluid flow rather than relying solely on proximal positive pressure.
architecture.expected_effect: Reduction in net pressure loss required from the proximal source to achieve target flow rates, while maintaining kink resistance and lumen patency because no structural changes are made to the tubing wall or internal geometry.
architecture.falsification_test: Measure the proximal inlet pressure required to maintain a constant volumetric flow rate through the multi-lumen tubing with and without the distal vacuum assist; if the proximal pressure requirement does not decrease by at least 10% under vacuum assist, the mechanism fails to address the pressure loss failure.
